techniques.evidence: src/app/api/mcp/route.ts:177 This is a tool server, not an agent runtime. Still, the rule's analogue holds here: tools/list and tools/call both work from the same per-request token scopes and plan gates, never from process env.

pairs.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
pairs.evidence: src/lib/athena/turn.ts:156 The user row is saved before the metered tool loop runs. If the loop throws, the turn only yields an error event. If the function is killed at maxDuration, nothing closes the row. Either way the generation is never closed as indeterminate, so the next turn's history() replays a question with no answer and no status.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/athena/turn.ts:156 An interrupted or failed generation leaves no closure record. Proposals do get one: athena-proposals-sweep.ts:68 stamps a stale claim with a first-class 'interrupted' kind and never retries it. That part conforms, apart from an extra ok:false failure flag next to the kind.

src/features/shared/athena/AthenaComposer.tsx:27 Typing a follow-up during a turn is allowed, but sending it is blocked (useAthenaThread.ts:106 also refuses). The text stays in the box and never joins the running tool loop at a model-call boundary. A durable turn record exists, so the 'refuse at the surface' exemption does not apply.

src/lib/athena/grounding.ts:174 Memory and skills gates are resolved per request. The tool roster is filtered from those values and execute() re-checks the same values at run time, so one policy drives both. Nothing reads process env.

src/app/api/cron/athena/deps.ts:7 The constitution she runs under has no writer, and the self-model is changed only by accepted diffs. Mutating tools are also left out of her roster (grounding.ts:141), so her governing inputs are outside her write reach.
src/app/api/cron/athena/deps.ts:159 No remote operation outlives a turn. The cycle makes one call with no tools, and turn tools are synchronous reads.
src/lib/athena/grounding.ts:120 The tool registry is compiled in. Nothing loads contributed code.
src/app/api/cron/athena/deps.ts:169 The cycle is a top-level cron run that creates its own thread. No run starts another run.
